items.Sentence: Preliminary Treatment at Headworks – Removes coarse solids (by bar screening), sand and silt (by grit removal) from wastewater.
Preliminary Treatment at Headworks – Removes coarse solids (by bar screening), sand and silt (by grit removal) from wastewater.
Primary Sedimentation – Removes solids from the wastewater by gravity. The heavier solids settle and are scraped out of the primary sedimentation basin.
Activated Sludge Biological Treatment – Activated sludge consists of microorganisms that consume non-settleable and dissolved organic contaminants which form a settleable floc.
Secondary Clarification – Removes biological floc from the wastewater which then mostly becomes part of the waste sludge.
Chemicals such as aluminum sulfate (alum) may be added as part of the treatment process to encourage floc formation and enhance solids removal.
Tertiary Treatment – The filtration process is used to remove or reduce suspended or colloidal matter from a liquid stream by passing the water through a bed of graded granular material.
The effluent to the microfiltration station is pretreated with sodium hypochlorite and aqua ammonia to prevent biofouling and then fed into automatic self-cleaning 500-micron strainers.

2 Million Gallon Microfiltration Equalization Tank – This equalization tank is adjacent to the Microfiltration Feedwater Wet Well and used to adjust the water level of the Microfiltration Feedwater Wet Well.

Reverse Osmosis (RO) – Prior to entering the RO process train, the pH of the treated water from the microfiltration units may need to be adjusted with sulfuric acid to protect the RO filters from calcium carbonate precipitation.

UV/AOP Disinfection – The AOP includes two (2) low-pressure ultraviolet (UV) irradiation trains and hypochlorous acid addition. The AOP is used to disinfect RO permeate and destroy some constituents of emerging concern (CECs).

The AOP effluent is stabilized and then distributed from the AWPF Pumping Station. Sodium hydroxide and calcium chloride are added in the Stabilization Tank to increase the pH of the AOP effluent to protect the LADPW’s distribution and injection system.
Six product water pumps in the Product Water Tank transfer the finished product water into the distribution system.

Sludge may be thickened, anaerobically digested, dewatered, and hauled to either the City’s Green Acres Farm located at Kern County for land application or to a contracted site in Arizona for composting and land application at various locations in Arizona and California.

Currently, the City is injecting on a daily basis approximately 248 tons of dry and dewatered biosolids at the TIRE injection facility: All of the Facility’s wet biosolids (up to 274,200 gallons per day containing approximately 73 tons of dry biosolids); and 175 tons of dewatered biosolids trucked from the Hyperion Wastewater Treatment Plant.

Sludge may be thickened, anaerobically digested, dewatered, and hauled to either the City’s Green Acres Farm located at Kern County for land application or to a contracted site in Arizona for composting and land application at various locations in Arizona and California. However, the land application option is currently unavailable.
The Sludge Blending Tank blends primary sludge and thickened waste activated sludge before it goes to the anaerobic digesters.

The Sludge Blending Tank is currently in a temporary configuration due to a failure of the center mixing shaft’s drive gearbox. The Discharger is temporarily using a pump for mixing in this tank until the gearbox is repaired or replaced.
